newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baer opens Frankfurt institutional office.
newsitem.headline: Baer opens Frankfurt institutional office.

text.p: Bank Julius Baer, the Swiss-based money management house, said Tuesday it has begun institutional investment operations in Frankfurt.
"In view of the anticipated growth in the sepcial fund business, the new company foresees favourable development opportunities," Baer said.
It added that proposed reforms in the German pension system are creating opportunities for private fund managers.

The Frankfurt operations, Julius Baer Kapitalanlage AG, opened on June 11 and will focus on managing special funds for foreign and domestic investors, especially for institutions such as pension funds, insurers or other groups.
The new company also will provide advisory services.
The operation "will enable the Julius Baer Group to further expand its position in the German market," Baer said.
Julius Baer manages roughly 70 billion Swiss francs in assets. It already has companies in Frankfurt, Geneva, London, New York and Hong Kong and other centres. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
